conventions.IsMinOn: IsMinOn f V p means for every y in V, f p <= f y. Membership p in V must be supplied separately when required.
conventions.EqOn: EqOn f g V means for every x in V, f x = g x.
conventions.Option: some p carries an X value; none carries no value.
conventions.implicit_scope: The production definitions and claims use arbitrary X : Type* and applicable implicit n : natural. a : V is a subtype point, not an arbitrary ambient point.

definitions.objects_spaces: Arbitrary type X, natural n, a family past : Fin n -> X -> real, and x : X. No topology, norm, measurability or cardinality structure on X.
definitions.quantifiers_order: For every X, n and past, C past is a real-valued function of x. The sum ranges over all Fin n indices.
definitions.conclusion: C past x is the sum of past i x over i = 0,...,n-1.
definitions.normalization_constants: An unweighted sum, not a mean; no division by n, regularizer, discount or additional term. For n=0 it is zero for every x.
definitions.information_use: Uses the value of every supplied past function at x.
definitions.boundary_excluded_regimes: Defined for every finite n and arbitrary real losses, including negative losses. It does not assert existence of any minimizer.

definitions.objects_spaces: A subset V of arbitrary X and past : Fin n -> X -> real; output is a subset of X.
definitions.quantifiers_order: For each x : X, membership M V past is tested by membership in V and comparison with every y in V.
definitions.assumptions: None; V may be empty and the cumulative objective need not attain an infimum.
definitions.conclusion: x belongs to M V past exactly when x belongs to V and, for every y in V, C past x <= C past y. IsMinOn supplies the comparison property; the separate membership conjunct enforces feasibility.
definitions.normalization_constants: Compares the raw sum C with the usual real non-strict order. Ties are allowed.
definitions.information_use: Only the cumulative objective values on V determine this set.
definitions.boundary_excluded_regimes: M can be empty on a nonempty set. At n=0, M equals V. This is an attained global minimum, not an infimum, local minimum, approximate minimum or uniqueness assertion.

definitions.objects_spaces: A subset V of arbitrary X and past : Fin n -> X -> real; output Option X.
definitions.quantifiers_order: For every V and past, branch on whether there exists an element of M V past.
definitions.assumptions: No nonemptiness or attainment assumption is required to define the function. The definition uses classical logic and choice in a noncomputable section.
definitions.conclusion: If M V past is nonempty, return some (Classical.choose h), where h witnesses that nonemptiness. Otherwise return none.
definitions.normalization_constants: No tie priority or numerical optimization tolerance is specified. some p and none are distinct Option constructors.
definitions.information_use: The selection is defined from the minimizer set; it has no sampled-feedback or sequential state input.
definitions.boundary_excluded_regimes: The definition is a total mathematical Option-valued function, not a certified executable solver. Nonempty V alone does not force some. Multiple minimizers do not force none, but the identity of the chosen tied minimizer is unspecified.

definitions.objects_spaces: V : Set X, a : V (a subtype element with a proof that its underlying point lies in V), loss : natural -> X -> real, t : natural; output Option X.
definitions.quantifiers_order: For each V, feasible a, full loss sequence and t, first branch on t=0; otherwise supply loss i.val for i : Fin t to S.
definitions.assumptions: The input a requires V to be inhabited. No condition on loss beyond real values.
definitions.conclusion: At t=0 return some of the underlying a. At t>0 return S V of the losses indexed 0,...,t-1.
definitions.normalization_constants: Zero-based indexing; t past losses are summed. The loss at t is not included. No normalization by t.
definitions.information_use: At zero uses a, at positive t uses the prefix of loss functions and V. It is a direct evaluation at t, not a recurrence through prior Option outputs.
definitions.boundary_excluded_regimes: Cannot be instantiated on empty V with a genuine a : V. Positive-time values may be none even though the zero-time value is some. Initial-point dependence is explicit at zero; for fixed V and loss the positive-time definition does not consult a.

example_context_definitions.meaning: The closed interval [0,1] in the reals, including both endpoints.
A subtype element of D with underlying real 3/4; the packet includes a membership proof.
A subtype element of D with underlying real 1/4; the packet includes a membership proof.
For every natural t and real x: (x-1/4)^2 if t=0, and (x-3/4)^2 otherwise, meaning every t>0.
For every natural t and real x: q t x if t<2, otherwise x+100, meaning every t>=2.
For every natural t and real x: q t x if x belongs to D, otherwise x+7. The branch is on feasibility, not time.
For every natural t and real x: x if t=0, otherwise x^2-x, meaning every t>0.

claims.objects_spaces: Arbitrary X, loss : natural -> X -> real, t : natural, x : X.
claims.quantifiers_order: For every loss, t and x.
claims.conclusion: C (i -> loss i.val) x equals the finite sum of loss i x over i in range t.
claims.normalization_constants: Both forms contain exactly indices 0,...,t-1, each once; both are zero at t=0.
claims.information_use: Only prefix values at x enter this equality.
claims.boundary_excluded_regimes: This reindexes a sum; it does not select an action or assert minimizer existence.

claims.objects_spaces: Arbitrary X, n, V : Set X, past : Fin n -> X -> real and p : X.
claims.quantifiers_order: For all V, past and p, conditional on the specified successful output.
claims.assumptions: h : S V past = some p.
claims.conclusion: p belongs to V AND for every y in V, C past p <= C past y.
claims.normalization_constants: Exact attained minimum of the raw finite sum, using <=.
claims.information_use: The objective contains all n supplied past functions.
claims.boundary_excluded_regimes: Conditional soundness only. It asserts neither that S succeeds for arbitrary inputs nor that p is unique.

claims.objects_spaces: Arbitrary X, n, V and past as above.
claims.quantifiers_order: For every V and past, an equivalence; its right-hand side negates existence of p : X with both stated properties.
claims.conclusion: S V past = none if and only if there does not exist p in V such that, for every y in V, C past p <= C past y.
claims.normalization_constants: Exact attainment, not boundedness below or existence of a real infimum.
claims.information_use: Uses feasibility and objective comparisons on V.
claims.boundary_excluded_regimes: Includes empty V and nonempty V with no attained minimum. Failure is not just emptiness and is not an algorithmic timeout. At n=0, failure is equivalent to V being empty.

claims.objects_spaces: Arbitrary X, n, V and two families past, pastprime : Fin n -> X -> real with the same index size.
claims.quantifiers_order: For every V, past and pastprime, assume for every i : Fin n and every x in V the two values agree.
claims.assumptions: h : for all i, EqOn (past i) (pastprime i) V, namely for all x in V, past i x = pastprime i x.
claims.conclusion: S V past = S V pastprime as Option values, including the exact selected point when successful.
claims.normalization_constants: No approximate equality, additive shift or rescaling premise is used.
claims.information_use: Values outside V may differ. Equality of each supplied function on V suffices for identical selection.
claims.boundary_excluded_regimes: No unique-minimizer assumption. This is stronger than merely equality of objective values at two separately chosen outputs. The stated hypothesis is pointwise equality per index, not just a partial observation history.

claims.objects_spaces: Arbitrary X, n, V, past and p : X.
claims.quantifiers_order: For all these objects, uniqueness quantifies over every q : X with q in V and the minimizer comparison property.
claims.assumptions: hp : p in V; hmin : for every y in V, C past p <= C past y; hunique : for every q in V, if for every y in V C past q <= C past y then q=p.
claims.normalization_constants: Exact unique feasible global minimizer, no strict convexity or quantitative gap required.
claims.information_use: All assumptions concern V and the cumulative objective on V.
claims.boundary_excluded_regimes: Sufficient conditions for a named output. The converse that every successful output is unique is not asserted. Outside-V points are excluded from the uniqueness quantifier.

claims.objects_spaces: Arbitrary X, V, a : V and loss : natural -> X -> real.
claims.quantifiers_order: For all V, feasible a and loss, at exactly t=0.
claims.assumptions: a carries membership in V; no loss hypotheses.
claims.conclusion: P V a loss 0 = some of the underlying a.
claims.normalization_constants: The branch is exactly zero, with no losses accumulated.
claims.boundary_excluded_regimes: Does not identify the empty-history S selection with a, and does not constrain a positive-time output.

claims.objects_spaces: Arbitrary X, V, a : V, loss, t : natural and p : X.
claims.quantifiers_order: For all inputs and t including zero, conditional on P V a loss t = some p.
claims.assumptions: The feasible initialization a and h : P V a loss t = some p.
claims.conclusion: p in V AND, for every y in V, sum over i in range t of loss i p <= sum over i in range t of loss i y.
claims.normalization_constants: Raw prefix sum over i<t. At zero all objective values equal zero.
claims.information_use: Only earlier losses appear in the minimized objective.
claims.boundary_excluded_regimes: Does not assert all positive-time outputs exist, uniqueness, regret, future optimality or performance on loss t.

claims.objects_spaces: Arbitrary X, V, a : V, loss and t : natural.
claims.quantifiers_order: For every such input and every t including zero, equivalence to absence of any feasible attained prefix minimizer.
claims.assumptions: The feasible initialization a; no attainment assumption.
claims.conclusion: P V a loss t = none if and only if there is no p in V satisfying, for every y in V, the prefix sum at p <= the prefix sum at y.
claims.normalization_constants: The prefix is exactly range t. At zero the objective is zero, a witnesses a minimizer, and both sides of the equivalence are false.
claims.information_use: Attainment is evaluated for the current prefix independently of earlier outputs.
claims.boundary_excluded_regimes: No persistence of failure, convergence, compactness or continuity theorem is asserted. Empty V is unavailable through the required a.

claims.objects_spaces: Arbitrary X, V, a : V, two loss sequences loss and lossprime, t : natural.
claims.quantifiers_order: For every input, assume for every natural s<t and every x in V, loss s x = lossprime s x.
claims.assumptions: h : for all s<t, EqOn (loss s) (lossprime s) V. V and the initial a are shared on both sides.
claims.conclusion: P V a loss t = P V a lossprime t as exact Option values.
claims.normalization_constants: The strict inequality s<t excludes index t as well as all later indices. At t=0 the hypothesis is vacuous.
claims.information_use: Changing losses at s>=t or values outside V cannot affect this equality when the specified prefix agrees on V.
claims.boundary_excluded_regimes: This is extensional prefix invariance for full functions on V. It is not a bandit-feedback implementability claim and does not assert equal outputs when initial points differ at zero.

example_checks.objects_spaces: X=real, D=[0,1], a=3/4, and the explicitly defined q sequence.
example_checks.quantifiers_order: A conjunction of seven top-level statements. The final conjunct quantifies over every natural t in range 3, then existentially selects p depending on t.
example_checks.assumptions: No theorem hypotheses; all objects are fixed by example definitions.
conclusion: a as a real equals 3/4.
P D a q 0 = some (3/4).
P D a q 1 = some (1/4).
P D a q 2 = some (1/2).
The real numbers 1/4 and 1/2 are unequal.
q 0 (1/4) is unequal to q 0 (3/4).
For every t in {0,1,2}, there exists p : real such that P D a q t = some p AND p in D AND, for every y in D, the sum over i<t of q i p <= the sum over i<t of q i y.
example_checks.normalization_constants: q 0 x=(x-1/4)^2; q t x=(x-3/4)^2 for every t>0. In the sixth conjunct the two values are 0 and 1/4. At t=2 the objective is 2(x-1/2)^2+1/8.
example_checks.information_use: Time one uses q 0; time two uses q 0 and q 1; time zero uses a.
example_checks.boundary_excluded_regimes: The last quantified assertion covers only t=0,1,2, not all times. The conjunction demonstrates distinct successive selected values and a nonconstant initial loss, but states no regret or future-performance bound.

example_checks.objects_spaces: D, a, q, qChanged as defined, all inputs real-valued.
example_checks.quantifiers_order: Three conjuncts, with differences evaluated specifically at time 2 and 3 and point x=0; output equality specifically at t=2.
conclusion: q 2 0 is unequal to qChanged 2 0.
q 3 0 is unequal to qChanged 3 0.
P D a q 2 = P D a qChanged 2.
example_checks.normalization_constants: qChanged t x=q t x for t<2; qChanged t x=x+100 for t>=2. Each displayed unequal pair is 9/16 versus 100.
example_checks.information_use: The changed losses start at the current index 2; the selection at time 2 uses only indices 0 and 1.
example_checks.boundary_excluded_regimes: No equality of selections at t=3 or later is asserted. The two difference checks do not quantify over all points.

example_checks.objects_spaces: D=[0,1], real point 2, q and qExtended, S with Fin 2, P at time 2.
example_checks.quantifiers_order: Five conjuncts. The third quantifies over every natural time t and every x in D through EqOn.
conclusion: The real point 2 does not belong to D.
q 0 2 is unequal to qExtended 0 2.
For every natural t and every x in D, q t x=qExtended t x.
S D (i : Fin 2 -> q i.val) = S D (i : Fin 2 -> qExtended i.val).
P D a q 2 = P D a qExtended 2.
example_checks.normalization_constants: qExtended t x=q t x when x in D and x+7 otherwise. The displayed unequal values at (0,2) are 49/16 and 9.
example_checks.information_use: Every loss agrees on the feasible region, though the extensions differ outside it; both displayed selections use two past functions.
example_checks.boundary_excluded_regimes: The displayed S and P equalities are for history length/time 2. The stronger all-times P equality is not itself a conjunct here, though claim9 can apply at other times.

example_checks.objects_spaces: D=[0,1], distinct endpoints 0 and 1, one past function constantly zero, S output p : real.
example_checks.quantifiers_order: Six conjuncts; the final existential requires one p satisfying all three inner conjuncts.
conclusion: 0 belongs to D.
1 belongs to D.
The real numbers 0 and 1 are unequal.
For every y in D, C of the single zero loss at 0 <= C of that history at y.
For every y in D, C of the single zero loss at 1 <= C of that history at y.
There exists p : real such that S D (the single zero loss) = some p AND p in D AND, for every y in D, C of that history at p <= C of that history at y.
example_checks.normalization_constants: The history length is 1, not 0. Its sole loss is zero at every real point, so the cumulative objective is constantly zero.
example_checks.information_use: The selector receives the constant history and D; no tie priority is supplied.
example_checks.boundary_excluded_regimes: Exhibits two distinct feasible minimizers and successful selection despite nonuniqueness. Does not specify p=0, p=1 or any other named tied point.

example_checks.objects_spaces: X=real, V=empty set, a single loss x -> x^2 and selector S.
example_checks.quantifiers_order: One equality, no quantified conjunct or P input.
conclusion: S on the empty real feasible set with the one-function squared-loss history equals none.
example_checks.normalization_constants: History length 1; ordinary square, with no additive term.
example_checks.information_use: The loss exists on the ambient reals but there are no feasible points.
example_checks.boundary_excluded_regimes: This uses S, which permits empty V. It cannot instantiate P with a feasible initial point on empty V. It is not a counterexample to minimization of x^2 on all reals.

example_checks.objects_spaces: D=[0,1], an empty history indexed by Fin 0, a=3/4, b=1/4 and q.
example_checks.quantifiers_order: Four top-level conjuncts; the first existential gives one p with two inner conjuncts.
example_checks.assumptions: No extra hypotheses; a and b each carry D membership.
conclusion: There exists p : real such that S D of the empty history = some p AND p in D.
P D a q 0 = some (3/4).
P D b q 0 = some (1/4).
P D a q 0 is unequal to P D b q 0.
example_checks.normalization_constants: Fin.elim0 defines a family on the empty Fin 0 index type; its sum is zero. Both P outputs are at exactly t=0.
example_checks.information_use: Empty-history S has no loss values to use; the two P evaluations explicitly use different initial subtype points.
example_checks.boundary_excluded_regimes: The first existential does not state a named output, and has no explicit IsMinOn conjunct. This check does not equate S on empty history with either initialization, and asserts no difference at positive times.

example_checks.objects_spaces: V=all reals, the identity loss x -> x, S with length 1, P initialized at real 0 using its universal-set membership proof.
example_checks.quantifiers_order: Six top-level conjuncts, with closedness in the real topology and convexity over the real scalar field.
conclusion: The universal real set is nonempty.
The universal real set is closed.
The universal real set is convex over the reals.
S univ of the single identity loss equals none.
P univ initialized at 0 with the loss sequence constantly equal to the identity function, at t=0, equals some 0.
The same P input at t=1 equals none.
example_checks.normalization_constants: The single cumulative loss is x itself. The initial point is 0; t=0 and t=1 are separate evaluations.
example_checks.information_use: At t=0 initialization suffices; at t=1 minimization of the first loss over all reals has no attained minimum.
example_checks.boundary_excluded_regimes: Nonempty, closed and convex feasibility alone does not ensure attainment for this loss. No compactness, boundedness or coercivity assumption is stated. The check is not a claim that every loss on such a set fails.

example_checks.objects_spaces: V=all reals, initial real point 0, sequence r : natural -> real -> real.
example_checks.quantifiers_order: Four top-level conjuncts. The last universally quantifies over every real x.
conclusion: P univ initialized at 0 with r, at t=1, equals none.
The same P input at t=2 equals some 0.
For every real y, the sum over i in range 2 of r i 0 <= the sum over i in range 2 of r i y.
For every real x, the sum over i in range 2 of r i x equals x^2.
example_checks.normalization_constants: r 0 x=x; r t x=x^2-x for every t>0. Thus at t=1 the objective is x, and at t=2 it is x+(x^2-x)=x^2.
example_checks.information_use: Each P evaluation recomputes from its complete current prefix. Failure at t=1 is not passed as state to t=2.
example_checks.boundary_excluded_regimes: An explicit recovery from no minimizer to an attained one. This rules out interpreting none as a permanent stopping state. No claim of eventual success for arbitrary sequences or any other time is stated.

productionClaims.header:
theorem claim1 (loss : ℕ → X → ℝ) (t : ℕ) (x : X) :
    C (fun i : Fin t => loss i.val) x = ∑ i ∈ range t, loss i x

theorem claim2 (V : Set X) (past : Fin n → X → ℝ) (p : X) (h : S V past = some p) :
    p ∈ V ∧ IsMinOn (C past) V p

theorem claim3 (V : Set X) (past : Fin n → X → ℝ) :
    S V past = none ↔ ¬ ∃ p, p ∈ V ∧ IsMinOn (C past) V p

theorem claim4 (V : Set X) (past past' : Fin n → X → ℝ) (h : ∀ i, EqOn (past i) (past' i) V) :
    S V past = S V past'

theorem claim5 (V : Set X) (past : Fin n → X → ℝ) (p : X) (hp : p ∈ V) (hmin : IsMinOn (C past) V p) (hunique : ∀ q ∈ V, IsMinOn (C past) V q → q = p) :
    S V past = some p

theorem claim6 (V : Set X) (a : V) (loss : ℕ → X → ℝ) :
    P V a loss 0 = some (a : X)

theorem claim7 (V : Set X) (a : V) (loss : ℕ → X → ℝ) (t : ℕ) (p : X) (h : P V a loss t = some p) :
    p ∈ V ∧ IsMinOn (fun x => ∑ i ∈ range t, loss i x) V p

theorem claim8 (V : Set X) (a : V) (loss : ℕ → X → ℝ) (t : ℕ) :
    P V a loss t = none ↔ ¬ ∃ p, p ∈ V ∧ IsMinOn (fun x => ∑ i ∈ range t, loss i x) V p

theorem claim9 (V : Set X) (a : V) (loss loss' : ℕ → X → ℝ) (t : ℕ) (h : ∀ s < t, EqOn (loss s) (loss' s) V) :
    P V a loss t = P V a loss' t

packet_headers_preserved.exampleContext:
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Basic
import Mathlib.Topology.Instances.Real.Lemmas
import Mathlib.Tactic

noncomputable section
open Set Finset Packet
namespace Examples

def D : Set ℝ := Icc 0 1

def a : D := ⟨3 / 4, by norm_num [D]⟩

def b : D := ⟨1 / 4, by norm_num [D]⟩

def q (t : ℕ) (x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  if t = 0 then (x - 1 / 4) ^ 2 else (x - 3 / 4) ^ 2

def qChanged (t : ℕ) (x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  if t < 2 then q t x else x + 100

def qExtended (t : ℕ) (x : ℝ) : ℝ := by
  classical
  exact if x ∈ D then q t x else x + 7

def r (t : ℕ) (x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  if t = 0 then x else x ^ 2 - x

end Examples

exampleChecks.header:
theorem check1 :
    (a : ℝ) = 3 / 4 ∧
    P D a q 0 = some (3 / 4) ∧
    P D a q 1 = some (1 / 4) ∧
    P D a q 2 = some (1 / 2) ∧
    (1 / 4 : ℝ) ≠ 1 / 2 ∧
    q 0 (1 / 4) ≠ q 0 (3 / 4) ∧
    (∀ t ∈ range 3, ∃ p, P D a q t = some p ∧
      p ∈ D ∧ IsMinOn (fun x => ∑ i ∈ range t, q i x) D p)

theorem check2 :
    q 2 0 ≠ qChanged 2 0 ∧
    q 3 0 ≠ qChanged 3 0 ∧
    P D a q 2 = P D a qChanged 2

theorem check3 :
    (2 : ℝ) ∉ D ∧
    q 0 2 ≠ qExtended 0 2 ∧
    (∀ t, EqOn (q t) (qExtended t) D) ∧
    S D (fun i : Fin 2 => q i.val) =
      S D (fun i : Fin 2 => qExtended i.val) ∧
    P D a q 2 = P D a qExtended 2

theorem check4 :
    (0 : ℝ) ∈ D ∧ (1 : ℝ) ∈ D ∧ (0 : ℝ) ≠ 1 ∧
    IsMinOn (C (fun _ : Fin 1 => fun _ : ℝ => 0)) D 0 ∧
    IsMinOn (C (fun _ : Fin 1 => fun _ : ℝ => 0)) D 1 ∧
    (∃ p, S D (fun _ : Fin 1 => fun _ : ℝ => 0) = some p ∧
      p ∈ D ∧ IsMinOn (C (fun _ : Fin 1 => fun _ : ℝ => 0)) D p)

theorem check5 :
    S (∅ : Set ℝ) (fun _ : Fin 1 => fun x : ℝ => x ^ 2) = none

theorem check6 :
    (∃ p, S D (fun i : Fin 0 => Fin.elim0 i) = some p ∧ p ∈ D) ∧
    P D a q 0 = some (3 / 4) ∧
    P D b q 0 = some (1 / 4) ∧
    P D a q 0 ≠ P D b q 0

theorem check7 :
    (univ : Set ℝ).Nonempty ∧ IsClosed (univ : Set ℝ) ∧ Convex ℝ (univ : Set ℝ) ∧
    S univ (fun _ : Fin 1 => fun x : ℝ => x) = none ∧
    P univ ⟨0, mem_univ 0⟩ (fun _ : ℕ => fun x : ℝ => x) 0 = some 0 ∧
    P univ ⟨0, mem_univ 0⟩ (fun _ : ℕ => fun x : ℝ => x) 1 = none

theorem check8 :
    P univ ⟨0, mem_univ 0⟩ r 1 = none ∧
    P univ ⟨0, mem_univ 0⟩ r 2 = some 0 ∧
    IsMinOn (fun x => ∑ i ∈ range 2, r i x) univ 0 ∧
    (∀ x, (∑ i ∈ range 2, r i x) = x ^ 2)
